findings.title: Negative queryset slicing is not supported by Django and will crash
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and a user-supplied cursor has a negative offset, this passes cursor.offset directly as a queryset slice start. Django querysets explicitly raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it. The OptimizedCursorPaginator path in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint is therefore a 500 for such cursors rather than advanced pagination, and cursors are attacker-controlled via Cursor.from_string.

findings.title: BasePaginator now allows negative offsets for prev cursors on all endpoints
findings.body: start_offset is only clamped with max(0, offset) when not cursor.is_prev; for is_prev cursors the raw user-supplied offset is used in queryset[start_offset:stop]. A crafted prev cursor with a negative offset makes Django raise AssertionError, turning normal paginated endpoints using BasePaginator into unhandled 500s. Previously offset was used as parsed too, but this change codifies/allows the negative case without validating it; offsets should be rejected/clamped for both directions.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime ordering used by its only caller
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint instantiates OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil directly on the attribute value and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged. For AuditLogEntry.datetime the value is a datetime, so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when build_cursor computes keys, and even if it did not, value_from_cursor would feed an int millisecond timestamp into build_queryset comparisons against a datetime column instead of converting like DateTimePaginator does. The optimized audit-log path is broken on the first page.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM and corrupts end_timestamp scores for duplicate spans
findings.body: The migration from SUNIONSTORE to ZUNIONSTORE uses the default aggregate SUM. If the same span payload exists in both the destination and merged set (retries/re-deliveries are expected in this consumer), its score becomes the sum of the two end_timestamp_precise values (~2x a Unix timestamp) instead of the span's end time. That corrupts eviction ordering in the same script: duplicated spans look far-future and are retained while non-duplicated earlier spans are popped. The union needs an explicit aggregate such as MAX (or weights 1,0 semantics) to preserve scores.

findings.title: Insert-time ZPOPMIN silently discards the earliest-ending spans from a segment
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, this pops span_count-1000 members with the smallest end_timestamp_precise scores with no metric, log, or dropped-segment marker. Those spans are permanently lost before flushing, so downstream receives an incomplete segment indistinguishable from a complete one; depending on timestamps this can drop children that ended early while keeping later spans. The previous Python-side behavior at least counted/logged oversized segments and skipped them explicitly rather than silently emitting a truncated segment.

findings.title: Removal of max_segment_spans guard lets oversized segments load unbounded at flush
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer enforces self.max_segment_spans; only the byte-size guard remains. Segments created before this deploy (plain Redis SETs are also incompatible, see zadd change), segments written by old consumers during a rolling deploy, or any path that bypasses the Lua cap can now accumulate arbitrarily many small payloads and be fully materialized into memory in payloads[key], risking consumer OOM instead of the previous counted/logged skip. The Lua hardcoded 1000 also ignores the configurable max_segment_spans=1001 setting.

findings.title: Changing span sets to sorted sets breaks in-flight segments stored as Redis SETs
findings.body: process_spans now issues ZADD and the Lua script issues ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN against span-buf:s:* keys, and _load_segment_data issues ZSCAN. Segments already buffered at deploy time are regular SETs (created by SADD/SUNIONSTORE) with a 3600s TTL; every one of these commands against them returns WRONGTYPE, failing process_spans/flush until the old keys expire and losing/delaying those in-flight segments. No migration, key versioning, or type handling is provided.

findings.title: Redirect chain traversal limit cut from 10000 to 1000 without justification
findings.body: The loop that follows span-buf:sr redirects to find the canonical segment set now stops after 1000 hops instead of 10000; the removed comment noted trees deeper than the limit may not be joined correctly. Deep segment trees between 1000 and 10000 redirects will be split into multiple segments (wrong segment_id/is_segment attribution downstream) — a silent correctness regression unrelated to the stated eviction optimization.

findings.title: New required end_timestamp_precise lookup can poison-batch on messages lacking it
findings.body: process_batch now does val['end_timestamp_precise'] unconditionally while constructing Span (and Span gained the field with no default). Any ingest-spans message missing that field — older producers, partially-formed spans, or schema variants previously accepted since only trace/span/project ids were read — raises KeyError for the whole batch, causing redelivery loops for that batch. Use a fallback (e.g. end_timestamp or message timestamp) or give Span a default.

findings.title: No test covers eviction, score preservation, or the new paginator
findings.body: The test changes only add the now-required end_timestamp_precise field to existing fixtures. Nothing exercises a segment exceeding 1000 spans (which spans get evicted, whether the root span survives), duplicate-payload merges preserving scores under ZUNIONSTORE, or OptimizedCursorPaginator/negative cursors. The core behavioral change of this PR — insert-time eviction — would pass CI even if it dropped the wrong spans or crashed.
